purpose: Which bioanalytical method produced the concentrations behind each kidney-function dataset the platform uses (reviewer's checklist O8), as each source reports it.
extraction: AI-assisted, 6 November 2026. Every quote was matched by script against the text of the PDF on the owner's computer (pdftotext, whitespace removed before comparison so that line and column breaks do not matter; the first Chen 2007 quote matched only with hyphens ignored, because the text layer drops the hyphen of 'R-' at a line end). Not yet reviewed by the platform owner.

studies.source: Chen N et al. J Clin Pharmacol 2007;47:1466-1475
studies.method: chiral LC/MS/MS (S- and R-lenalidomide); separate ultrafiltration LC/MS/MS method for protein binding
quotes: Plasma and urine samples were analyzed for S- and R-lenalidomide concentrations by a validated chiral liquid chromatography/tandem mass spectrometry (LC/MS/MS) method.

The R- and S-lenalidomide standard curves were linear from 5 to 200 ng/mL in plasma and from 100 to 20 000 ng/mL in urine. The lower limit of quantification of lenalidomide was 5 ng/mL in plasma and 100 ng/mL in urine.
Between-day precision was within 6.1% in plasma assays and within 4.5% in urine assays. Assay accuracy was 97.3% to 99.7% for plasma samples and 92.7% to 103.7% for urine samples.
The lenalidomide standard curve was linear from 0.3 to 300 ng/mL. The lower limit of quantification was 0.3 ng/mL. Intraday precision was within 5%, and assay accuracy was 87.4% to 94.5%.
studies.note: The last quote is the protein-binding (ultrafiltrate) method. The upper end of the plasma curve (200 ng/mL) is below the peaks reported in the study (group mean Cmax up to 765 ng/mL), so samples above it would need dilution; the paper does not describe this.

Calibration curves were constructed over a range of 5–1,000 ng/mL

intra-assay bias (%) and precision (%CV) below 7.86% and 5.01%, and inter-assay bias and precision below 6.05% and 10.55%, respectively. The method was fully compliant with FDA and MFDS bioanalytical method validation guidance.
